answer: Each agent can receive only a small, nontransferable influence allowance per epoch, earned by completing randomly assigned tasks that require consistent behavior over time. A newcomer’s votes count little until it builds a track record, while the same allowance cannot be multiplied by creating more accounts. A sybil attacker must therefore keep many identities active through repeated checks and tasks, paying the real cost of labor and resources on every voyage from the wharf to the summit of influence.
